headline: President Mohammed Shahabuddin resigns from office
summary: The President has submitted his resignation to the Speaker of the National Parliament, leaving the position vacant.
details: President Mohammed Shahabuddin has stepped down from his position as the head of state, submitting his resignation letter to the Speaker of the National Parliament, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed.

Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, who had cut short his personal visit to Thailand to return to the country, will officially announce the details during an emergency press conference at the Parliament's oath room today at 5 PM.
According to Article 54 of the Constitution, the Speaker will perform the duties of the President until a new president is elected to fill the vacancy.
Under Article 123 of the Constitution, a new president must be elected by the members of Parliament within 90 days of the office becoming vacant.
The BNP is expected to nominate a candidate for the presidency as the majority party in Parliament.
Mohammed Shahabuddin took office on April 24, 2023, and his term was originally scheduled to continue until April 2028.
caption:
Bangladesh's President Mohammed Shahabuddin has resigned. The Speaker of the National Parliament now takes over the duties.

President Mohammed Shahabuddin has stepped down from his position as the head of state, submitting his resignation letter to the Speaker of the National Parliament, Hafiz Uddin Ahmed.

Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmed, who had cut short his personal visit to Thailand to return to the country, will officially announce the details during an emergency press conference at the Parliament's oath room today at 5 PM.

According to Article 54 of the Constitution, the Speaker will perform the duties of the President until a new president is elected to fill the vacancy.

Under Article 123 of the Constitution, a new president must be elected by the members of Parliament within 90 days of the office becoming vacant.

The BNP is expected to nominate a candidate for the presidency as the majority party in Parliament.

Mohammed Shahabuddin took office on April 24, 2023, and his term was originally scheduled to continue until April 2028.

headline: Couple critically burned in Savar home explosion while lighting mosquito coil
summary: A husband and wife, both garment workers, suffered severe burns after a gas leak caused a blast in their rented home.
details: A man and his wife were critically injured in a home explosion in the Majidpur Dighirpar area of Savar late Thursday night.
The victims, identified as 28-year-old Md. Kawsar and 24-year-old Ruby Akter, are both employees at local garment factories.
The blast occurred around 1:00 AM when Kawsar attempted to light a mosquito coil using a gas lighter, triggering an immediate explosion that engulfed the room in fire.
According to Dr. Shaon Bin Rahman of the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery, Kawsar suffered burns over 100% of his body, while Ruby suffered burns over 88%.
Kawsar's father, Siman Sheikh, stated that there was no direct gas connection inside the room, but a connection existed outside by the window.
Sheikh believes that gas may have leaked from the external line and accumulated in the room, leading to the accident.
Neighbors rushed to the scene after hearing the victims' screams, controlled the fire, and rescued the couple.
Savar Model Police Station Inspector Nur Mohammad stated that the police have not yet been formally notified of the incident but are currently investigating the matter.
